description: Why a construct signature is keyed `new()` and not `new`. `WidgetFactory` declares both — a construct signature and a property somebody really called `new`, which is ordinary TypeScript — and they are two members with two colors. `WidgetFactory#new()` colors the construction and leaves the property floored; a segment spelled `new` would have put both under one key and colored the property from an entry written for the constructor.

diagnostics.message: Call to `widgets.new` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay, override or baseline entry colors it, so it is assumed to throw. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@no-throw/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.
